title: Protesters attack theatre director over play about Mahatma Gandhi in Bengaluru

tea.why: Protesters objected to a play's portrayal of Mahatma Gandhi, accusing it of spreading misinformation and containing anti-Gandhi references.
tea.want: Protesters demanded legal action against the theatre director, actors, and others associated with the play.
tea.changed: Oct 31: Protesters disrupted the play's staging, smeared ink on the director's face, and lodged a formal police complaint.

summary: On Saturday in Bengaluru, a group of protesters disrupted the staging of a play about Mahatma Gandhi's assassination at the Suchitra Film Academy in Banashankari. The demonstrators allegedly smeared ink on the face of the play's writer and director, Addanda C. Cariappa, and confronted him over the production's content. Organised by Rangabhoomi Trust (R), Kodagu, the play faced objections for its dialogues, references to the Partition, and the portrayal of Mahatma Gandhi. Complainants, led by Kushal Hanumegowda, filed a formal complaint at the Banashankari police station seeking legal action against the director and cast. Reports also noted the involvement of Congress workers in the protest.
demands: Legal action against the play's director and actors
Investigation into alleged black-market ticket sales
response: According to the sources, a complaint has been lodged at the Banashankari police station and investigations are underway.

updates.text: Protesters disrupted a play at Suchitra Film Academy, smeared ink on the director's face, and filed a police complaint.
